When trained to output **tempo as well as beats and downbeats**, the proposed model reaches a **beat F-measure of 86.2** and a **downbeat F-measure of 69.8**. These are beat-level F-scores from Table 4, which sits on p. 5 and is discussed in Section 3.3.3 on p. 6. They are the best results in that table.

| Model (output data) | Beat f | Downbeat f |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (beat, downbeat) | 66.9 | 57.6 |
| Proposed (beat, downbeat) | 85.7 | 63.3 |
| Proposed (beat, downbeat, tempo) | **86.2** | **69.8** |

- **Effect of adding tempo:** it raises beat F from 85.7 to 86.2 and downbeat F from 63.3 to 69.8. The authors say this "suggests a benefit of joint learning" (p. 6).
- **Metric:** the beat-level F-measure follows the standard beat and downbeat tracking benchmark, with a ±70 ms tolerance (p. 4).
- **Row label:** the table labels this row "Proposed (d, db, t)". The caption defines only b (beat), db (downbeat) and t (tempo), so "d" is probably a typo for "b".
- **Scope:** Table 4 reports only F-scores. The document gives no precision or recall for this comparison.
